subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 35-year-old woman with bipolar II disorder has been stable on a mood stabilizer. Her new primary care physician, unaware of the diagnosis, starts her on an SSRI for residual depressive symptoms. Over the next several weeks she develops decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, and increased energy, and begins making grandiose plans.
question: Which of the following best explains this clinical deterioration?

options.text: SSRIs are ineffective for depression and should be replaced with a typical antipsychotic
Mood stabilizers lose efficacy over time and must be discontinued
Antidepressants can destabilize mood in bipolar disorder and may precipitate a manic or hypomanic episode
This represents an adverse effect of the mood stabilizer requiring an increased dose
These symptoms indicate the development of schizophrenia

explanation_correct: In bipolar disorder, antidepressant therapy can destabilize mood and precipitate manic or hypomanic episodes; bipolar disorder also carries a high suicide risk. Treatment relies on mood stabilizers — lithium, lamotrigine, valproate, and carbamazepine — together with atypical antipsychotics. Her new SSRI is the most likely trigger, and it should be stopped while mood-stabilizer therapy is optimized.

explanation_incorrect.A: SSRIs can be effective for depressive symptoms, but in bipolar disorder they risk mood destabilization; a typical antipsychotic is not the appropriate explanation or solution.
explanation_incorrect.B: Mood stabilizers do not simply wear off in this fashion; the temporal relationship to SSRI initiation points to antidepressant-induced destabilization.
explanation_incorrect.D: The symptoms began after adding an SSRI, not after changing the mood stabilizer, so increasing the stabilizer dose is not the primary explanation.
explanation_incorrect.E: New onset of elevated mood, decreased sleep, and grandiosity in a patient with bipolar disorder represents a mood episode, not schizophrenia.

educationalObjective: Antidepressants can destabilize mood in bipolar disorder; maintenance treatment uses mood stabilizers and atypical antipsychotics, and suicide risk is high.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 24-year-old woman reports lifelong mood variability. Since adolescence she has had numerous periods lasting days to weeks when she feels mildly down, fatigued, and less interested in activities, alternating with periods when she feels unusually energetic, confident, and productive. Neither extreme has ever caused her to miss work or required hospitalization. She has never had a full major depressive or manic episode. This pattern has persisted for 6 years.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Bipolar II disorder
Cyclothymic disorder, because mild hypomanic and depressive symptoms have been present for at least 2 years
Major depressive disorder
Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia)
Borderline personality disorder

explanation_correct: Cyclothymic disorder is a milder form of bipolar disorder in which the patient fluctuates between mild depressive and hypomanic symptoms. It requires at least 2 years of symptoms present at least half the time, with any remission lasting no more than 2 months, and no full major depressive, manic, or hypomanic episode. Her 6-year pattern of mild mood swings without marked impairment fits this diagnosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Bipolar II requires at least one full major depressive episode and one hypomanic episode; she has never had a full episode of either.
explanation_incorrect.C: Major depressive disorder requires at least 2 weeks of five or more depressive symptoms and does not account for her alternating hypomanic periods.
explanation_incorrect.D: Persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) involves at least 2 years of at least two depressive symptoms but only depressed mood, not alternating hypomanic symptoms.
explanation_incorrect.E: Borderline personality disorder involves instability in mood, relationships, and identity with impulsivity, not the cyclic mild hypomanic and depressive pattern described.

educationalObjective: Cyclothymic disorder requires at least 2 years of mild depressive and hypomanic symptoms present at least half the time with remission of 2 months or less and no full mood episodes.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 31-year-old man has had mood fluctuations for 4 years. He has many periods of 2 to 5 days of mild elevation with increased energy and productivity, alternating with 1- to 2-week periods of mild sadness and low energy. He has also had one distinct 3-week episode of depressed mood, anhedonia, guilt, fatigue, and poor concentration that met full criteria for a major depressive episode. He has never had a manic episode.
question: Which of the following best distinguishes the appropriate diagnosis from cyclothymic disorder?

options.text: The presence of at least one full major depressive episode with hypomanic symptoms establishes bipolar II disorder rather than cyclothymia
Cyclothymia is diagnosed whenever mood symptoms last more than 2 years, regardless of full episodes
Bipolar I disorder is required because any mood episode has occurred
The absence of psychotic features excludes a bipolar spectrum disorder
Persistent depressive disorder is the correct diagnosis because depressive symptoms predominate

explanation_correct: Cyclothymic disorder involves at least 2 years of mild hypomanic and depressive symptoms that never meet full criteria for a manic or major depressive episode. This patient has had a full major depressive episode along with hypomanic symptoms and no history of mania, which establishes bipolar II disorder — a hypomanic episode plus a major depressive episode with no manic episode. The full major depressive episode is the key finding that excludes cyclothymia.

explanation_incorrect.B: Duration alone is not sufficient for cyclothymia; symptoms must never reach full manic or major depressive episode criteria, and his major depressive episode does.
explanation_incorrect.C: Bipolar I disorder requires at least one manic episode; he has never had mania, only hypomanic symptoms and a major depressive episode.
explanation_incorrect.D: Psychotic features are not required for a bipolar spectrum diagnosis; their absence does not exclude bipolar II.
explanation_incorrect.E: Persistent depressive disorder requires at least 2 years of depressive symptoms without hypomanic episodes; his hypomanic periods and full major depressive episode point to bipolar II.

educationalObjective: A full major depressive episode plus hypomanic symptoms and no mania indicates bipolar II disorder, whereas cyclothymia never reaches full mood episode criteria.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 40-year-old woman with bipolar I disorder has had two manic episodes requiring hospitalization. She is being discharged, and her psychiatrist is selecting a maintenance pharmacologic regimen. She has a family history of suicide and has previously expressed hopelessness during depressive episodes.
question: Which of the following treatment choices is most appropriate for this patient?

options.text: An SSRI as monotherapy for mood stabilization
A typical antipsychotic as first-line maintenance therapy
Benzodiazepines for long-term mood stabilization
Ketamine infusions as first-line maintenance treatment
A mood stabilizer such as lithium, lamotrigine, valproate, or carbamazepine, often with an atypical antipsychotic

explanation_correct: Bipolar disorder is treated with mood stabilizers — lithium, lamotrigine, valproate, and carbamazepine — and with atypical antipsychotics. Antidepressants can destabilize mood and are avoided as monotherapy. Patients with bipolar disorder have a high suicide risk, so maintenance treatment and close monitoring are essential.

explanation_incorrect.A: Antidepressant monotherapy can destabilize mood in bipolar disorder and is not appropriate for maintenance treatment.
explanation_incorrect.B: Atypical, not typical, antipsychotics are used in bipolar disorder; typical agents are not first-line maintenance therapy.
explanation_incorrect.C: Benzodiazepines may be used briefly for agitation or insomnia but are not mood stabilizers and carry a risk of dependence.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ketamine is used in treatment-resistant depression, not as first-line maintenance therapy for bipolar disorder.

educationalObjective: Bipolar disorder is maintained on mood stabilizers such as lithium, lamotrigine, valproate, or carbamazepine and atypical antipsychotics, not antidepressant monotherapy.
